answer: Divergent Audit Path Sampling.** Each identity is assigned a unique deterministic audit path through a shared grove of task records; honest agents complete and sign their assigned path, while duplicates must maintain every cloned identity's path simultaneously. Collision checks compare path signatures against a per-epoch sonnet of expected traversal orders, so any two identities sharing a source diverge detectably. An attacker pays full compute and storage for every clone, plus the karst of repeated path reconciliation—cost scales linearly with clone count, making duplication self-revealing.
